title: Copilot Studio: conversational set-up of connector connections with in-chat sign-in
summary: The briefing leaves the applicability of blocking maker-provided credentials open, although Microsoft documents that this control requires end-user credentials at runtime for all tools in affected environments. The roadmap facts, connector-blocking navigation path and PowerShell command are supported.

claims.claim: The related end-user connection experience is documented in the Microsoft Copilot harness tool documentation.
claims.quote: An agent created with the Microsoft Copilot harness. ... When a tool signs in with each user's own account, users set up their connection the first time the agent needs it.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: An agent that needs a connection the user has not set up pauses and displays a Connection Required card.
claims.quote: When the agent needs a connection you haven't set up, it pauses and shows a Connection Required card.

claims.claim: The Connection Required card has Set up connection, Retry and Deny buttons.
claims.quote: The card has the following buttons: ... Set up connection ... Retry ... Deny

claims.claim: Set up connection opens the agent's Manage your connections page.
claims.quote: Set up connection | Opens the Manage your connections page for the agent.

claims.claim: The documented setup procedure connects each item the action needs and then returns the user to the chat.
claims.quote: On the Manage your connections page, connect each item that the action needs. ... Return to the chat.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Manage your connections lists tools, flows and AI models in the agent that use the user's own account.
claims.quote: The Manage your connections page lists the tools, flows, and AI models in the agent that use your own account.

claims.claim: For these tools, the agent acts using the user's own connection rather than a shared account.
claims.quote: Some tools in a Microsoft Copilot Studio agent sign in with each user's own account instead of one shared account. Before the agent can use one of these tools for you, you need to connect your account.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Connections are saved separately for each agent.
claims.quote: Connections are saved for each agent and each channel.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Connections are channel-specific, so users of the same agent in several channels set them up in each channel.
claims.quote: Connections are saved for each agent and each channel. If you chat with the same agent in more than one channel, set up your connections in each channel.

claims.claim: In Microsoft Teams, the agent automatically retries the action after the user connects.
claims.quote: In Microsoft Teams, the agent retries the action automatically after you connect. If it doesn't, or if you closed the dialog without connecting, select Retry on the card.

claims.claim: Create or pick connections lets the user select an existing connection or create a new one for each service.
claims.quote: In the Create or pick connections dialog, for each service under Name, select an existing connection under Connection, or create a new one.

claims.claim: Users can remove their connections from the agent with Disconnect.
claims.quote: Above the list, select Disconnect. ... The connections are removed for this agent in the channel where you chat with it, such as Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Disconnecting cannot be undone.
claims.quote: You can't undo this action. The next time the agent needs one of these connections, it asks you to set it up again.

claims.claim: Expired means the connection sign-in expired or was revoked.
claims.quote: Expired | Your sign-in for the connection expired or was revoked. | Renew: Sign in again.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Stale means the agent changed after the user connected and the connection needs review.
claims.quote: Stale | The agent changed after you connected, so the connection needs to be reviewed. When you open the page, it tries once to restore the connection automatically.

claims.claim: Deny cancels the action.
claims.quote: Deny | Cancels the action.

claims.claim: After Deny, the agent does not try the action again.
claims.quote: The agent doesn't try the action again and tells you that it was canceled.

claims.claim: The response to an unattended Connection Required card, specifically, is not documented in the researched Learn material.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Connection Required unattended autonomous. Opened end-user-connections, end-user-manage-shared-agent and configure-no-maker-authentication; none specifies the unattended handling or timeout of that chat card.

claims.claim: A tool blocked by a data policy cannot be selected in the Microsoft Copilot harness tool-adding experience.
claims.quote: When a data policy blocks a tool, the tool appears unavailable in the Add a tool panel and you can't select it.

claims.claim: Publishing an agent using a policy-blocked tool can fail.
claims.quote: The message explains that your organization's data policy blocks the tool, so the tool can't be used, even by an agent, and publishing or running an agent that uses it can fail.

claims.claim: Running an agent using a policy-blocked tool can fail.
claims.quote: The message explains that your organization's data policy blocks the tool, so the tool can't be used, even by an agent, and publishing or running an agent that uses it can fail.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; summary; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies can prevent agent makers from using specified Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.claim: Data policies govern agents in the environments included in the policy scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Whether data policies are evaluated again at the precise in-chat sign-in step is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio in-chat data policy connections. Opened admin-data-loss-prevention, add-tools-custom-agent and end-user-connections; they document general scope, real-time enforcement and blocked tools, not a separate policy evaluation at this sign-in step.

claims.claim: The printed Power Platform admin center path reaches connector blocking in a new data policy.
claims.quote: select Security, and then select Data and privacy. ... Select Data policy. ... select New Policy ... select the environment in the Available tab, and then select Add to policy. ... The Assign connectors page appears. ... Select the three dots ... select Block.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy accepts PolicyName, Classification and Connectors and assigns or moves the specified connectors to the policy group.
claims.quote: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy [-PolicyName] <String> [-Classification] <String> [-Connectors] <Object[]> ... If any of the connectors are already classified in a different group, they are moved to the specified group.

claims.claim: Classification Blocked puts connectors in the Blocked data-policy group.
claims.quote: Allowed values are 'General', 'Confidential', and 'Blocked' (for Non-business, Business, and Blocked, respectively).

claims.claim: Existing data policies can be changed using Edit Policy.
claims.quote: To edit an existing data policy, select the data policy and select Edit Policy.

claims.claim: Configuring the data policy requires administrative rights over the applicable scope.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator can configure the data policy control.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin ... Data policies ... View and manage tenant policies | Yes ... View and manage environment policies | Yes

claims.where: Open questions: data policies and blocking maker-provided credentials
claims.claim: Whether blocking maker-provided credentials applies when a user connects in chat remains an open applicability question.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime. ... When an end user interacts with an agent ... and triggers a tool action, the agent prompts that user to sign in if they haven't already.
claims.fix: Replace the Open questions bullet 'Do data policies and the blocking of maker-provided credentials apply when a user connects in chat? Watch the Learn data policy page.' with 'Are data policies evaluated again at the in-chat connection step? Watch the Learn data policy page.' General credential-control applicability is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/configure-no-maker-authentication.
